title: Actual exam question for Salesforce's Slack-Consultant exam
question: During a governance workshop for a new Enterprise Grid launch, the IT Security Lead argues that all Slack apps should be blocked by default to prevent data exfiltration. Conversely, the Head of Product argues that this will create a bottleneck that stifles innovation and slows down the team. To facilitate a consensus that satisfies both security and speed, which approach should the consultant recommend?
option_A: Configure the App Management settings to pre-approve a curated list of popular apps and enable a streamlined App Request flow for all others, designating specific workspace owners as reviewers to distribute the workload.
option_B: Grant the Head of Product full 'Org Owner' privileges so they can bypass approval requirements, while keeping the restriction in place for standard users.
option_C: Enable a policy that allows all apps but restricts the scopes they can request, effectively blocking high-risk apps automatically.
option_D: Implement a sandbox workspace where users can install any app for testing, but strictly enforce an 'Admin Approval' workflow for all apps in the production workspaces.

option_D: Implement mandatory Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) for all workspace members and guests.
